results.market_title: Will the U.S. invade Iran before 2027?
results.reasoning: A major US-Israel-Iran war has been raging since February 2026 (airstrikes killing Khamenei, naval blockade, missile exchanges, huge US military buildup), and Pentagon plans for 'ground operations' were drafted as early as March 2026, but as of October 2026 there is no evidence of a US ground offensive intended to seize or control Iranian territory — reporting explicitly notes plans 'fall short of a full invasion.' Trump stated on 8 October 2026 that the US will not resume strikes before the 3 November midterms, leaving roughly two months before the 31 Dec 2026 deadline for an invasion to be launched. Given nearly a year of intense conflict has already occurred without crossing the ground-invasion/control threshold, and political reluctance to escalate to occupation, 'No' remains more likely than not, though the extreme volatility and active blockade/strikes keep meaningful invasion risk alive.

results.market_title: Will Jeremiah Smith win the 2026 Heisman Trophy?
results.reasoning: As of mid-October 2026 (roughly Week 6-7), Jeremiah Smith is the clear betting favorite for the Heisman (around -210 to -220, implying ~68-69% market-implied win probability) after back-to-back 200-yard games, well ahead of QB contenders like Darian Mensah, Keelon Russell and Gunner Stockton. However, more than half the season remains, wide receivers have won the Heisman only rarely (most recently DeVonta Smith in 2020) due to voter bias toward quarterbacks, and in-season favorites at this point historically do not convert at the full rate implied by betting lines once injury risk, voter fatigue, and QB-driven team success in November are factored in. Discounting the betting-implied probability for these structural factors suggests Smith's true win probability is closer to 58-62%, making the 'No' (he does not win) outcome roughly 38-42%.
results.key_findings: ["Jeremiah Smith (Ohio State WR) is the betting favorite at -210/-220 to win the 2026 Heisman as of early-mid October (BetMGM, SI, Oddschecker)","Smith has posted back-to-back 200-yard receiving games and leads major Heisman Watch rankings (Eleven Warriors, Covers.com)","Only one wide receiver-primary player (DeVonta Smith, 2020) has won the Heisman in the modern era, reflecting historical QB voter bias","More than half of the regular season remains as of mid-October, leaving ample time for standings to shift among QB contenders like Darian Mensah, Keelon Russell, Gunner Stockton and CJ Carr"]

results.market_title: Will the National Rally group hold 10 French Senate seats after the 2026 election?
results.reasoning: RN currently holds only 3 Senate seats and has never had a Senate group (minimum 10 needed). Party leadership itself frames the goal as "doubling or tripling" its seats to "approach" (frôler) ten — aspirational language suggesting even RN's own optimistic internal target sits near, not comfortably above, the threshold. Municipal 2026 results reportedly boosted RN's local implantation (grand électeur base), with LR reportedly bracing to lose 3-5 seats to RN's push, which is a real tailwind, but France's indirect senatorial electoral system (dominated by mostly rural/small-commune grand électeurs) has historically been unfavorable to RN relative to its national vote share, making a clean breach of 10 seats and formal group registration by Oct 12, 2026 uncertain rather than likely.
results.key_findings: ["RN holds just 3 Senate seats currently (as of pre-2026 election), insufficient to form a group (Wikipedia FR)","RN campaign director Ludovic Pajot: party wants to 'double or triple' its senator count, i.e., 'frôler' (approach) ten seats (Public Sénat)","Post-March 2026 municipal elections, LR fears losing 3-5 Senate seats to RN's momentum (Public Sénat, dated late March 2026)","As of Sept 13, 2026 (2 weeks before the Sept 27 vote), no confirmed final seat count or group declaration exists yet","RN has never had a Senate group in its history; forming one would be a major symbolic and organizational milestone tied to Le Pen's 2027 presidential strategy"]

Unfilled makers are missed trades, not losses.

xvenue.read: polyMoves = minutes where Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c; staleKalshi = of those, Kalshi's same-minute quote was still crossable after its 7.000000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (avgStaleEdgeC = cents of edge per share); kalshiSameMin/NextMin = Kalshi moved the same way that minute / the next; kalshiLeads = Kalshi moved first and Polymarket followed. A Kalshi lane is worth building only if staleRate x avgStaleEdgeC is meaningfully positive over many games. us* = the same for Polymarket US (taker 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p)); kUsCross = minutes where buying on one US-legal venue and selling on the other cleared both taker fees (the only fully legal arbitrage pair for a US operator).
